title: As Easy as A–B–C–D: Diagnosing Coherence Before Collapse
description:
This paper defines a four-step procedural method for applying The Bridge diagnostic. It enables independent observers to classify system stability using only publicly observable evidence.
The method is procedural only. It introduces no new laws, diagnostics, variables, interpretations, or governing conditions.
ABCD Diagnostic Procedure
A — Internal Coherence
Assess whether commitments, decisions, actions, and outcomes remain aligned. Persistent internal misalignment indicates instability independent of external conditions.
B — Constraint Alignment
Assess whether stated constraints actually govern observed outcomes. Misalignment between rules and behavior indicates constraint failure.
C — Fragmentation Under Load
Assess whether misalignment amplifies under pressure into rule proliferation, inconsistency, or corrective escalation. Amplification indicates coherence loss.
D — Trajectory
Assess whether the system’s trajectory is stabilizing or degrading across successive observations. Sustained degradation indicates closure of corrective capacity.
Output
The procedure produces:
diagnostic classification only
observer-invariant conclusions
no prediction, prescription, or interpretation
Each step constrains the next. Skipping steps invalidates the diagnosis.
Scope Limits
This method:
does not predict outcomes
does not prescribe intervention
does not assign causation or blame
It evaluates coherence state only.
Canonical Note
This procedure is a direct operationalization of The Bridge and is fully compatible with DiamondLogic: The Governing Rule of Relational Stability Under Load. No additional primitives are introduced.
